checks.evidence: I read PgAttachments.put at e5c02f7. It runs `select 1 from infrx.jobs where request_id=%s and org_id=%s for update` (no row = NotFound), then reads the binding. An exact (handle, digest) list in order commits as a no-op, anything else is Conflict, and it inserts only when the job is unbound. Connections are autocommit plus an explicit `begin`, so the isolation is READ COMMITTED and the read after the lock sees the committed rows. Probe: process A bound R1,R2 through MediaStaging.attach. A real second OS process (probe_child.py, a fresh PgAttachments over the same d6 database) then got the same results on BOTH images (plain and INFRX_D1_IMAGE=supabase): exact 'ok'; superset, reorder, subset, same handle with another digest, and (R1,R1) on the bound job each 'Conflict:state_conflict'; a foreign org's ref 'NotFound:not_found'. A get after every attempt returned [R1,R2]. Through the port, (R1,R1) on an unbound job raised InvalidRequest invalid_request. Serialization, both images: while another connection held the row `for no key update`, a `for key share` (the foreign-key check's lock mode) was acquired at once, and `for update` got LockNotAvailable under lock_timeout=1s. The head put in a second process was still waiting after 3 s and finished 'ok' only after the holder rolled back (elapsed 2.81 s). A copy with attach_not_serialized did not wait (0.068 s). Concurrent race, two OS processes putting (R1,) and (R2,) on the same fresh jobs: head 0/21 both-committed and 21/21 exactly one (plain and supabase); the attach_not_serialized mutant 7/7 (plain) and 6/7 (supabase) both-committed, leaving 2-ref bindings nobody attached. `INFRX_MUTANTS=all pytest -rs tests/m/test_pilot_mutants.py` on d6 plain: '40 passed in 154.62s', no skips. Hand-applied in copies: rebind_to_a_superset_accepted -> test_mpilot_pg__an_attach_is_write_once_and_tenant_bound 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class infrx.contracts.errors.Conflict>' at test_pilot_media.py:593 (the superset iteration); attach_not_serialized -> test_mpilot_pg__an_attach_waits_for_the_job_row 'AssertionError: the attach did not wait for the job row' at :637. Pristine: both pass. Supabase, the ten _pg and relay cases: '10 passed, 14 deselected'.

I ran the exported media_parity__an_attach_is_write_once (driver v2_driver.py) on the fake (mediastore_factory), MediaStaging (test_store.factory), MediaPreparation (test_prepare.conformance_factory), MediaUploads (test_uploads.conformance_factory) and the store alone (MediaUploads, attachments=None): all PASS. On PostgreSQL, test_mpilot_pg__the_exported_mpilot_cases_run_on_postgresql passed on both images. contracts quick: 640 passed. Also fake_attach_accepts_a_duplicate -> fake 'an attach of one ref twice was accepted'; in_process_duplicate_accepted -> all four real adapters report the same.

Each case read and hand-mutated in a copy. replay_read_unguarded -> test_mpilot__a_replay_whose_attach_record_is_unreachable_is_retryable: 'AssertionError: b'{"error":{..."code":"internal_error"...}}' / assert (500, 'internal_error') == (503, 'depend..._unavailable')'. attached_with_no_media_reads_unbound -> test_mpilot__a_text_job_attached_here_is_bound_whatever_the_record_holds: 'infrx.contracts.errors.NotFound: not_found: no staged media for job ...' (the text job's own preparation, as the evidence declares). bound_here_before_it_is_durable -> test_mpilot__a_failed_durable_attach_binds_nothing_here[unreachable] and [conflict]: 'AssertionError: assert '00000001-...' not in {...: (MediaRef(...),)} = MediaUploads.by_job'. Extra mutant of my own (the _resume gate `is not None` -> truthiness) is killed by the text-job case (400 == 200) and by two existing G cases. The same behaviour on real PostgreSQL across a restart (probe test_v3): a media job attached by process A is read back by a restarted adapter with PG up. Then a relay World (CREDIT) with PgAttachments composed accepted a job whose answer was lost, w.restart(), and the record was made unreachable two ways (a closed port, and `docker pause` of my own infrx-d6-postgres). The real get raised psycopg.OperationalError (ConnectionTimeout, its subclass, when paused). The same-key replay answered '503 dependency_unavailable; job.state=preparing outcome=None by_job={}' in both. Limit: the World's jobs are the fake store, so the relay-level job was a text job; the media binding over PG was shown at the adapter level.

Direct probe (test_v4) at e5c02f7. A ref whose digest shares the file's first 16 hex (same path) -> NotFound. mtime now+30 s and +59 s -> served; +61, +90 and +3600 s -> NotFound. A symlink at the path to the right bytes -> NotFound, and served again once restored. No cache root -> 'NotFound not_found'. Hand-applied in copies: disk_hash_compared_by_prefix -> 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE NotFound' at test_pilot_media.py:313 (the collided ref); disk_symlink_followed -> the same at :318 (the symlink); future_mtime_believed -> the same at :324 (the future mtime); disk_lookup_without_a_root -> 'infrx.contracts.errors.DependencyUnavailable: dependency_unavailable: no processing cache is configured' where NotFound is expected. Each dies at its own assertion.

The 15 skips are 12 test_s3.py cases, 2 test_s3_mutants.py cases and the empty PG mutant parametrization. With my MinIO on 55724: '431 passed, 2 skipped'. The delta is +14 run (the 12 S3 cases and the 2 S3 mutant tests all pass); the one extra skip is test_parity's corpus cache, absent from my /tmp clone, whose 7 cases pass with CORPUS_CACHE set. INFRX_M_S3_LOCAL_CREDS does not exist in the tree: test_s3's s3_env supplies the MinIO literals itself. contracts quick: '640 passed in 7.15s'. tests/g quick (the 7 files): '176 passed, 2 warnings in 22.37s'. `git diff --stat 2d1dcbe e5c02f7` touches only research/plan/evidence/m/MPILOT-078eefe.md (75+/12-). Spot-checked three table rows against the commits: 2972df1 touches attachments.py, store.py, fakes/media.py, support.py and services.py, plus the named cases and mutants; 8a31e6c is tests only (pilot_mutants.py, support.py, test_pilot_media.py), matching 'cases only'; 2d1dcbe touches prepare.py and adds the four named disk mutants and the no-root case. Every mutant and case the table names exists in pilot_mutants.py, contracts/mutants.py and test_pilot_media.py. One attribution slip is reported as N2.

The evidence lists as open, not fixed: Limit 8 (the gateway's own index is not re-verified, and a symlinked directory is followed), Limit 7 (deleting a previous incarnation's expired files across a restart), Limit 1 (a zero-ref attach leaves no row) and Limit 5 (MediaCollector is not composed and protects only in-process state). The 'Left, stated' paragraph repeats all four. The code matches: ProcessingCache.get trusts an own-index entry without re-hashing, sweep() walks only self.entries, and `grep -rn 'MediaCollector('` finds nothing in infrx/ outside gc.py. Grepping the fix-round diff finds no comment claiming any of the four fixed. The text-job case says outright that the record has no row and pins only the in-process side. support.Durable's comment says 'an attach of no media leaves no row (Limit 1 of MPILOT)'. No case asserts cross-process cache deletion, own-index re-verification or collector protection.

findings.claim_broken: Ruling (d) in the evidence: 'any other binding - other refs, a superset, a subset, a reorder, none - is 409 conflict'. Across processes on PostgreSQL, 'none' over a durably bound job is accepted. Limit 1 discloses only the opposite direction (media attached elsewhere over a job attached here with none).
findings.evidence: Probe test_v1_write_once_across_processes, plain and supabase: process A binds R1,R2 on d6. A fresh adapter (adapter_for(tmp_path), attachments=the same PgAttachments, nothing in memory) calls attach(job, ()) and it is accepted. Output: 'fresh-process attach(()) over durably-bound job: ACCEPTED; fresh.attached -> () ; durable.get -> [med_e943..., med_b9a8...]'. That process now treats a media job as bound to no media. The relay does not reach this: _resume attaches only when attached() is None, and a fresh admission has a new job id.
findings.minimal_fix: Either state it in Limit 1 and in ruling (c)/(d) (a zero-ref attach is not checked against a durable binding made by another process), or in MediaStaging.attach, when refs are empty and attachments is composed, raise Conflict if `await self.attachments.get(job_id)` is not None.

findings.claim_broken: The row attributes the attachments.py wording ('staged_media keeps a handle's first description') to 'this commit' (e5c02f7), but e5c02f7 touches only the evidence file.
findings.evidence: `git log -S "keeps the FIRST description" -- apps/infrx-api/infrx/media/attachments.py` -> 2972df1. `git diff --stat 2d1dcbe e5c02f7` -> only research/plan/evidence/m/MPILOT-078eefe.md.
findings.minimal_fix: In that row, name 2972df1 for the attachments.py docstring wording.

findings.claim_broken: 'One attach naming the same ref twice is invalid_request in every adapter' (Limit 9) holds at the MediaStore port. The record itself (PgAttachments.put) answers an untranslated driver error. Its only caller checks first, so this is informational.
findings.evidence: Probe: a second process calls PgAttachments.put(unbound_job, (R1,R1)) -> 'RAW psycopg.errors.UniqueViolation: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "job_media_pkey"'. It rolls back (a later get is None). Through MediaStaging.attach the same input is 'InvalidRequest invalid_request'. On a bound job the record answers Conflict.
findings.minimal_fix: None needed while MediaStaging.attach is the only caller. Optionally reject duplicate handles at the top of PgAttachments.put with errors.InvalidRequest.
